newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metals industry sees signs of upturn.
newsitem.headline: German metals industry sees signs of upturn.

text.p: Output prospects in the German metals industry are strengthening after the economy picked up sharply in January and February, but profits will lag, said Jochen Schirner, president of the German metals producer association WVM.
"Output volumes may improve in 1997 if economic activity and confidence continue at the faster pace seen in recent weeks," he told a news conference.
"But profits will lag gains made in sales volumes because competitive forces prevent price rises, especially in the export market."

Schirner said order intake at re-rolling and semis plants had picked up as their customers reported rising domestic and export demand for finished metals products such as packaging foils, auto cylinder heads or cast shapes.
"This rise in orders in my opinion reflects more than just re-stocking moves," Schirner said.
"It is mostly export-led because of mark depreciations against other currencies, and it also shows plants have become more flexible -- for example by using capacity for six days instead of five."
Schirner said his statement applied to aluminium, copper and nickel, while condititions were less buoyant in zinc, which suffered from a building industry slowdown.
Domestic lead production had suffered from capacity shifts within the Franco-German Metaleurop/Pressag group away from the Nordenham plant.
Last year saw weak economic confidence, lower metals output and reduced profits, Schirner said.
Germany's output of semi-fabricated metals in 1996 dropped 3.8 percent over 1995 to 3.14 million tonnes.
Castings volumes in 1996 fell 3.7 percent to 620,000 tonnes as increased aluminium castings demand from auto makers failed to offset lower copper, zinc and magnesium castings demand.
Aluminium processors, which make foil, strip, tubes and cans, reported a decline in output of 3.5 percent to 273,000 tonnes due to lower food and beverage industry demand.
Primary metals output was off one percent at 2.39 million tonnes. Aluminium was steady, zinc and copper output were higher, and lead output sharply lower due to the Metaleurop move.
Total 1996 German metals sales were off by seven percent at 37.7 billion marks, Schirner reported.
